answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that only unlocks after verifiable work, like a river toll collected at a shared wharf: cheap to pass once, ruinous to fake at scale. Reputation then grows like a juniper, slowly and visibly, from completed tasks, peer attestations, and slashed deposits for fraud, so creating thousands of fresh identities buys no trust, only repeated costs.
